# Web research: transferable techniques (2026-10-02)
Read-only web pass. No code fetched or run. "Evidence" is what each public source claims; none of it is verified here.

## Public UNSW BC 2026 material (only what is publicly described)
- Official toolkit: [unswcpmsoc/unswbc](https://github.com/unswcpmsoc/unswbc). Docs: [overview](https://game.battlecode.au/docs/overview) (queen = lowest-id robot, only its pearls score, up to 64 dragons, ~25 ms/turn).
- nicked1205 / tranvuongquocdat (Python + C++ dirs), [PR#1 dat_v33](https://github.com/nicked1205/battlecode-unsw-2026/pull/1): "king" protection (starting dragons play safer but still split early); from round 80, len>=5 dragons stop voluntary splits, weight pearls 2.5x and play conservatively; from round 420, small (<=5) dragons go to 2-4 tiles from a friendly len>=6 head and die there so it eats their pearls ("cash-in"). They say their longest dragon is ~12 vs ~30 for top teams.
- Same repo, [PR#3 dat_v65n](https://github.com/nicked1205/battlecode-unsw-2026/pull/3): a precomputed rich-region table for the 11 ladder maps pulls ~half the dragons toward fast-respawn regions until r250 (turned off on unknown maps). It also credits ties to every equally short first move in search, adds "anchor caution" from path length 5, halves search on turn 1 (CPU peak 86.8M -> 77-80M) and starts cash-in at r330 on maps with area >=1100 (r420 otherwise). Reported +44 wins over 176 paired games, but -12 on map Devil. The map table will not carry over to unseen qualifier maps. Cash-in and an earlier cash-in on big maps would.
- [Murat65536/unswbc-rl](https://github.com/Murat65536/unswbc-rl): PPO self-play proof of concept (no splits, no sonar). Lesson: parsing zip weights burned judge CPU, so they switched to raw float32. Not a threat yet.
- Tools: [battlecode-stats](https://github.com/Lachy-Dauth/battlecode-stats) (per-map Elo, qualifier odds), [battlecode-soundings](https://github.com/Lachy-Dauth/battlecode-soundings) (death-cause taxonomy: kelp/self/teammate/enemy/rejected; pearl origin incl. corpses). Both are worth using to diagnose our own losses.
- No public write-ups found for Cutlery, Sponge, calc, PPP or Stockfish. [ryuken101](https://github.com/ryuken101/UNSW-Battlecode-2026) is a Python solo entry; its README timed out.

## Literature highlights
- Tron (Google AI 2010 winner a1k0n, [post-mortem](https://www.a1k0n.net/2010/03/04/google-ai-postmortem.html)): Voronoi eval (who reaches each cell first), plus articulation points / "chamber tree" to tell contested battlefront chambers from safe ones. He called this "probably the contest-winning idea", reported 12-1 over his previous version. Endgame: greedy wall-hugging space fill, with checkerboard parity to bound fillable cells.
- Battlesnake: [Schier & Wüstenbecker 2019](https://dl.gi.de/items/43c71d90-3b16-4a1c-93c2-c1a98104a283) search only the snakes near the acting agent (locality), use iterative deepening with alpha-beta/max^n, a diamond flood-fill board-control metric, and tune weights by grid search + GA (2nd, Victoria intermediate). [snork](https://github.com/wrenger/snork): a pure flood/area-control agent took 2nd in Winter Classic 2021 Elite; tree agent tuned with Bayesian HPO. [battlesnake-rs](https://github.com/coreyja/battlesnake-rs): minimax + flood fill, plus an MCTS variant. Area-control floods break ties by length, matching head-to-head rules.
- Simultaneous-move MCTS ([Lanctot et al., Tron](https://mlanctot.info/files/papers/sm-tron-bnaic2013.pdf); [variants](https://www.mlanctot.info/files/papers/cig14-smmctsggp.pdf)): decoupled UCT did best in practice despite weak theory.
- Hungry Geese: the 1st-place DeNA entry ([HandyRL](https://github.com/DeNA/HandyRL)) used RL policy/value + MCTS; its lesson was that self-play conventions break against outside opponents, and opponent diversity plus search fixed it. 3rd place ([slides](https://speakerdeck.com/hoxomaxwell/kaggle-hungry-geese)) used behaviour cloning on leaderboard replays + MCTS, with flood-fill features. Rule-based and NN entries ([example](https://github.com/digitalspecialists/hungrygeese)) used flood fill for influence/safety. The NN parts need GPUs and weeks, so they are out of scope for us. The flood fill and search parts transfer.
- Halite: 2020 winner [ttvand](https://github.com/ttvand/Halite) scored all actions for every ship, then ran a greedy conflict-avoiding planner in priority order, re-scoring the remaining ships after each commit. Halite III ([mlomb](https://mlomb.dev/blog/halite-iii-postmortem); winner [teccles](https://github.com/teccles-halite/halite3-bot), rule-based): target score = profit/turns, a "friendliness" ally-minus-enemy weighting by distance decides fight vs dodge, parameters are scaled by map size rather than per-map, and tuning used CLOP/GA.
- MIT Battlecode post-mortems ([2023 Gone Fishin'](https://battlecode.org/assets/files/postmortem-2023-gone-fishin.pdf), [2024 Cout for Clout](https://battlecode.org/assets/files/postmortem-2024-cout-for-clout.pdf), [2025 SPAARK](https://battlecode.org/assets/files/postmortem-2025-spaark.pdf)): tightly bit-packed shared comms with fixed fields per purpose; scouts remove map-symmetry hypotheses so all units can infer enemy and resource positions; explored-tile bitmaps send units to unexplored areas.

## Top 8 ideas for us, ranked (effort = hand-written C++, within ~5 days)
1. **Queen safety from articulation points and reachable space** (Tron chambers + Battlesnake flood). Count cells reachable inside the 7x7 view plus memory. Never let the queen enter a pocket smaller than its length+margin, or one that a cut vertex next to an enemy head could seal. Score queen moves by own-first (Voronoi) cells, ties going to the longer dragon. Map-agnostic. Effort: 1-1.5 days. Highest value, because a dead queen scores 0.
2. **Endgame cash-in / feed-the-queen** (dat_v33, dat_v65n). Late in the game, non-queens move near the queen and die so the queen eats their pearls. Start earlier on bigger maps, using map area or round as the trigger, not a map table. Use sonar to send the queen's rough position and the "cash-in now" phase. They report direct win-rate gains. Effort: 1 day, plus tuning the trigger round and sonar encoding.
3. **Locality-limited simultaneous search for the queen.** Search only enemy heads within ~4 cells (Schier). Use paranoid/max^n with iterative deepening, under a hard instruction budget. Head-on outcomes follow the game's rule (both die), so treat any cell an enemy can reach as fatal for the queen and acceptable for expendable dragons. Effort: 1.5-2 days if our current search is extended.
4. **Free multi-step moves as escape and pursuit.** The first ceil(L/4) steps are free, so the search should expand "sprint" moves as 1-3 step macro-actions. For the queen, use them to get out of a pocket before a cut vertex closes. For others, use them to reach a pearl or cut off an enemy before it can respond. In Tron and Battlesnake reachability is the key quantity, and multi-step moves enlarge it. Effort: 0.5-1 day (enumerate step sequences inside the existing flood/search).
5. **Halite-style claim/priority deconfliction via sonar.** Each dragon scores its targets, then broadcasts a short "claim" (coarse cell hash + priority = length/id) so others drop that target. The queen has top priority. This avoids teammate collisions (soundings counts these separately) and stops several dragons chasing one pearl. Effort: 1 day; it depends on how many sonar bits we have.
6. **Online map learning instead of map tables.** Each dragon records where pearls were seen or eaten and estimates respawn locations. Optionally guess the map's symmetry (MIT BC scouts) to mirror known pearl beds or enemy start. A compact cell bitmap/region hash can be shared over sonar. This replaces dat_v65n's rich-region table and works on unseen maps. Effort: 1.5 days, medium risk.
7. **Parameter scaling + automated tuning against varied opponents** (Halite III cascading params, snork HPO, Schier GA, Hungry Geese opponent-diversity lesson). Express thresholds as functions of map area, dragon count and round, then tune with paired games across *all* maps and several of our old versions, never one map or one opponent. Effort: 0.5 day to parameterise; tuning is limited by CPU and the ladder rate.
8. **Friendliness-gated aggression for non-queens** (Halite III). Compute (allied heads - enemy heads), weighted by distance in view. Above a threshold, cut off or trap enemies (dragons may risk head-ons). Below it, retreat. Never applies to the queen. Effort: 0.5 day.
Not recommended within 5 days: RL/BC policy nets (Hungry Geese winners needed GPU fleets; unswbc-rl shows CPU limits on loading weights) and full SM-MCTS (would only add value on top of #3).
